verdict.label: not_comparable
verdict.rationale: Side A reports a randomized trial in varenicline-treated overweight/obese smokers comparing a low-carbohydrate diet with a moderately fat-reduced diet, finding no between-diet difference in weight change at 12 weeks (-0.2 vs 0.5 kg, not statistically significant). Side B reports a network meta-analysis of overweight/obese adults comparing low-carbohydrate and low-fat diets against a standard hypolipemic diet, finding the low-carbohydrate diet significantly reduced weight versus the standard hypolipemic diet (MD -6.31 kg, indirect evidence). The contrasts differ: A compares low-carbohydrate vs moderately fat-reduced diet, while B compares low-carbohydrate vs standard hypolipemic diet. The populations also differ materially: A is restricted to smokers attempting cessation with varenicline, whereas B is a general overweight/obese adult population without this restriction. These differences in comparator and population prevent a direct comparison of the findings.

source_evidence.quote: In a randomized clinical trial, 122 men and women smokers with body mass index 25-40kg/m(2) were assigned low-carbohydrate versus moderately fat-reduced diets.

Mean weight changes for the low-carbohydrate versus fat-reduced groups were -1.2 (SD 2.2) versus -0.5 (SD 2.0) kg, -0.2 (SD 3.3) versus 0.5 (SD 2.6) kg, and 2.2 (SD 4.5) versus 2.1 (SD 3.9) kg at 4, 12, and 24 weeks after the target quit date, respectively (not statistically significant).

Indirect evidence revealed that both the low-carbohydrate diet (MD = -6.31 kg, 95% CI: -11.23, -1.39) and the low-fat diet (MD = -5.61 kg, 95% CI: -10.61, -0.61) significantly reduced weight among overweight/obese adults compared to the standard hypolipemic diet.

diagnostics.notes: Side A: comparator is moderately fat-reduced diet; population is varenicline-treated smokers. Side B: comparator is standard hypolipemic diet; population is general overweight/obese adults. Different comparators and populations preclude direct comparison.
